newsitem.title: UK: ASDA pulls Alka Seltzer over price upset.
newsitem.headline: ASDA pulls Alka Seltzer over price upset.

text.p: British supermarket group ASDA Plc said on Thursday it had withdrawn stomach upset treatment Alka Seltzer, made by Germany's Bayer AG, after being told by a court to comply with a 10 percent price rise.

"We do not believe a price increase of five times the rate of inflation can be justified," said ASDA coprporate counsel Nick Cooper. "We would rather not stock the product than pass on such a price rise to our customers."
ASDA has been involved in a long-running battle against resale price maintenance (RPM) in over-the-counter medicines.
This is the system whereby drug companies can force retailers to sell products at set minimum prices.
ASDA said Bayer had objected to ASDA's refusal to increase the 30-tablet pack price on Alka Seltzer and had obtained a court injunction against the supermarket chain.

"We are disappointed with the ruling," Cooper added. "We believe RPM is anti-competitive and anti-consumer, and this price rise is a classic example." Britain's Office of Fair Trading has been investigating RPM in healthcare products and is expected to decide shortly whether to refer the issue to the restrictive practices court.
